facts.condition: For a receiver-skew channel, whenever conditioning on the shared coordinating variable separates all use-indexed auxiliary/input packets, the optimal block Marton score equals the one-use optimum repeated once per channel use.

After choosing a tuple representation for a cross-use-coupled candidate, its midpoint-score residual has an exact entropy-dependence decomposition; a positive residual requires the favorable dependence terms to strictly outweigh the associated conditioning penalties.

assumptions: All relevant alphabets are finite, and candidate auxiliaries obey the channel Markov constraint.
No conclusion is assumed for unrestricted cross-use coupling or for the root program's terminal capacity objective.
The block channel is memoryless across uses.
The midpoint score assigns equal weight to the two receiver-common terms.
